supportClaimEffect: bounded opt-in generated graph only; no general DWG support claim

authority.oda: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1 sections 9, 20.4.44, 20.4.45 and 20.4.54 define the HEADER dictionary reference, dictionary/default references and layer plotstyle hard pointer.

api: A separate optional DRW_DwgDefaultPlotStyleProvider interface selects synthesis after the caller's writeDwgClasses callback and receives planned dictionary/placeholder identities. It does not add virtuals to DRW_Interface or change public entity, facade or DRW_Interface layout. Existing consumers and providers returning false follow the unchanged default path. Early or late competing plotstyle-root registration fails the output transaction. Consumers must not supply opaque records claiming ownership of generated identities; such hidden references are not validated by this slice.
implementation: Reserve two distinct identities after caller reservations; register the root and DICTIONARYWDFLT class instance before HEADER/CLASSES. HEADER points to the root. After caller OBJECTS, emit NOD-owned DICTIONARYWDFLT with one Normal soft-owner entry and matching hard-pointer default, and the corresponding dictionary-owned ACDBPLACEHOLDER. Only the internally synthesized layer 0 gets the placeholder hard pointer; supplied layer records remain untouched. Validate NOD/frame and class-instance completion before publication. Existing raw/opaque and arbitrary graph closure rules remain separate.
collision_and_rollback: Reject existing or late root collisions, NOD/GROUP aliases to the protected placeholder, caller DICTIONARY or DICTIONARYWDFLT ownership/default aliases to either generated identity, and caller impersonation of the generated dictionary. Root aliases are case-insensitive for the reserved ASCII key. Failed graph staging restores the allocator and admission/class state before a planning notification; checkpoint-copy exceptions leave state unchanged. Deferred-object emission is checkpointed; an injected exception after the dictionary frame rolls back bytes, class/identity ledgers and completion state, and same-writer retry succeeds. If rollback itself cannot allocate, a sticky internal error prevents publication; the same low-level writer is not claimed retryable in that extreme condition.

focused_tests.result: PASS across AC1015/1018/1021/1024/1027/1032 for no-provider and disabled-provider defaults; generated graph and following LINE; reserved identities; caller layer-0 override; preexisting unrelated owner; early/late root conflicts; late NOD/GROUP alias; nested DICTIONARY/DICTIONARYWDFLT alias and impersonation; object/entity identity collisions; existing-destination preservation and same-facade retry. Direct controls cover class ordinal collision, planned-identity reservation, stage retry/high-water restoration, admission/emission checkpoint exceptions, injected post-dictionary exception, class ledger and same-writer retry. HEADER handle streams are walked directly for R2007+. Exact synthetic-versus-caller DICTIONARYWDFLT null-role bytes and following references are checked across all six versions; the typed-null distinction applies to AC1015.
focused_tests.consumer_guard: lc3_compat_check object target compiled against the optional interface.
focused_tests.independent: LibreDWG 0.14 independently decoded all six physical scratch files using tests/dwg_default_plotstyle_libredwg.py: HEADER hard pointer to NOD child, Normal soft-owner and default hard-pointer to PLACEHOLDER, placeholder soft-pointer owner to dictionary, LAYER 0 hard pointer to placeholder, and one following LINE. R2004+ class instance count is 1; AC1015 does not serialize this count.
focused_tests.reproduction: Run libdxfrw_dwg_default_plotstyle_optin_tests --keep and pass its OUTPUT directory plus a dwgread binary to tests/dwg_default_plotstyle_libredwg.py. Only locally authored scratch files are generated.

limits: This is explicit opt-in, not automatic synthesis. The synthetic core graph is checked; hidden references in arbitrary opaque records, broader document closure, native consumer/platform behavior, class/producer breadth and general ODA conversion remain open. The other five version-specific ODA failures do not become support claims. The provider must avoid hidden competing ownership of planned identities. No DWG/DXF fixtures are committed.
